successCriteria.description: The token storage persists the bearer token in sessionStorage: setToken writes it, getToken reads it back, clear removes it, and getToken returns null when no token is stored. The token must survive a page reload (sessionStorage semantics) and must NOT be written to localStorage or held only in memory.

Every authenticated API call attaches an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header when a token is present in storage, and omits the header when no token is present (e.g. the public login call). This is verifiable by a unit test that stubs fetch and asserts the request headers.

On a 401 response, the API client clears the token via the injected ITokenStorage and throws an ApiError with status 401, so callers can route to login. A unit test asserts sessionStorage is empty after a 401 and that the thrown error carries status 401. No JWT `exp` claim is decoded client-side.

The API client exposes typed methods returning the Phase 1 shared types: login → LoginResponse, getMe → EmployeeProfile, getLeaves → LeaveRequestView[], getLeave → LeaveRequestView, getBalances → LeaveBalanceView[]. Each method's return type is the imported shared type (not a locally re-declared shape).

Non-2xx responses (other than the 401 path) surface a typed ApiError whose `message` is sourced from the backend `error` field and `code` from the backend `code` field, with `status` set to the HTTP status code. A unit test asserts a 404/400 response body `{ error, code }` maps to ApiError with matching message/code/status.
`npm run build` in web/ completes with zero TypeScript errors (strict mode, noUnusedLocals, noUnusedParameters) and `npm test` passes, including the Authorization-header and 401-clears-token tests.

constraints: Persist the bearer token in sessionStorage only — never localStorage and never in-memory only. The token must survive a reload and be cleared on tab close.
Detect unauthorized access solely from the server's HTTP 401 response. Do NOT decode the JWT `exp` claim (or any JWT payload) client-side to determine expiry.
Use the native fetch API; do not add a new HTTP client dependency (axios or similar).
Satisfy strict TypeScript: no unused imports/locals/parameters, strict null checks, no `any` (use `unknown` with type guards).
Import LoginResponse, EmployeeProfile, LeaveRequestView, LeaveBalanceView (and any related enums) from web/src/shared/types/index.ts — do not re-declare or duplicate these shapes locally.
The login call is public and must NOT attach an Authorization header (no token is sent on login).
Do not log tokens, passwords, or PII (GP-004).
outOfScope: No auth session/context, login UI, route guards, or redirect-to-login behavior — those belong to Phase 3/5. This phase only provides the API client + token storage primitives.
No create/submit/approve/reject/cancel leave operations or any state-changing endpoints — only the read endpoints listed in the phase scope.
No client-side JWT decoding/expiry logic and no token refresh mechanism.
No changes to the Vite dev proxy or backend — the existing /auth, /employees, /leaves, /balances proxies already cover these endpoints.

entityInvariants.invariant: The token storage is the single owner of bearer-token persistence. It exposes exactly getToken/setToken/clear; getToken returns null when absent; setToken overwrites any prior token; clear removes it. All persistence goes through sessionStorage.

ApiError is a typed error carrying message (string), status (number), and optional code (string). It is the only error type the API client throws for HTTP failures, so callers can branch on status/code without string-matching.

The API client is the single place that attaches the Authorization header and handles the 401-clears-token behavior. It is constructed with an ITokenStorage and never reads sessionStorage directly. On 401 it clears the token and throws ApiError(status 401); on other non-2xx it throws ApiError with the backend error/code mapped.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Non-2xx throws ApiError with status and backend error/code mapped.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The API client's typed method return types must reuse the canonical shared types (LoginResponse, EmployeeProfile, LeaveRequestView, LeaveBalanceView) rather than re-declaring them.
ApiError's message/code mapping must match the backend error contract `{ error: string; code: string }` — `error` maps to message, `code` maps to code, and the HTTP status maps to status.
The barrel must re-export IApiClient, ApiClient, ITokenStorage, TokenStorage, and ApiError so later phases import from the public entry point only.
Tests must run under the existing Vitest/jsdom configuration (globals enabled, setupTests.ts loaded) — no new test runner or config.

integrationPoints.why: Source of the canonical LoginResponse, EmployeeProfile, LeaveRequestView, LeaveBalanceView types the API client returns.
The API client's typed methods are the web client's contract against these endpoints; response shapes and the { error, code } error contract must match.
These later phases consume IApiClient and ITokenStorage from the barrel; the interfaces must be stable and complete for their constructors.
